title: Parental, gestational, and early-life exposure to indoor environmental hazardous factors on allergic rhinitis among preschool children in Urumqi City: a case-control study.
ehr_evidence: Questionnaires were developed for all children in the case group and control group... the questionnaires were completed by the parents or other guardians of the children at home.
summary: A case-control study of 2020 preschool children in Urumqi City, China, examining associations between parental, gestational, and early-life indoor environmental exposures and allergic rhinitis.
key_findings: Cesarean section was a risk factor for childhood AR (OR = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.02-1.67, P < 0.05).
Father with AR was a risk factor for childhood AR (OR = 2.67, 95% CI = 2.08-3.44, P < 0.01).
Mother with AR was a risk factor for childhood AR (OR = 3.70, 95% CI = 2.88-4.74, P < 0.01).
Mother with asthma was a risk factor for childhood AR (OR = 3.11, 95% CI = 1.18-8.20, P < 0.05).
Newly purchased furniture in the parents' residence during pregnancy was a risk factor for childhood AR (OR = 1.49, 95% CI = 1.03-2.14, P < 0.05).
Passive smoking, petkeeping, house plants, and indoor dampness/mold were not significantly associated with AR in the final model.
population: Preschool children (mean age ~5.2 years) in Urumqi City, China; 404 physician-diagnosed AR cases and 1616 matched controls across 60 kindergartens.
exposure_domain: indoor environmental exposures (indoor air quality, formaldehyde/new furniture, passive smoking, pets, house plants, dampness/mold)
limitations: Case-control design with strict physician-diagnosed case definition may be overly conservative and introduce selection bias.
Parental report of exposures introduces recall bias.
Exposure assessment was largely retrospective, limiting causal inference.
Some environmental factors (passive smoking, pets, dampness) were not confirmed as associated, possibly due to design and outdoor air quality changes from the 'coal to gas' project.
data_availability_statement: The datasets generated and/or analyzed during the current study are not publicly available due to the data belonging to the School of Public Health of Fudan University but are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
